concept_summary: A restaurant at 659 Columbus Ave in the North Beach NCD seeks to expand from 1,486 sq ft to 2,820 sq ft with tenant improvements, limited cooking, no alcohol service, and recorded music.

overall.line: Of the 3 approvals this concept needs: 1 further review (zoning and use), 1 insufficient information (building permit and change of use), 1 allowed (health permit).
overall.next_step: Request a written Letter of Determination from San Francisco Planning to confirm whether Planning Code §780.3(c)(1)(B) prohibits this expansion, and whether any variance or exception pathway exists, before signing the lease or filing any application.

findings.text: An active Type 47 on-sale general eating-place license has been on file at 659 Columbus Ave since May 2021.
findings.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

findings.text: Planning Code §780.3(c)(1)(B) provides that a new restaurant in the North Beach Special Use District may be approved by Conditional Use on the first story only if the Zoning Administrator first finds the space is currently or was last legally occupied by a restaurant or bar, that use was not discontinued or abandoned, and the new restaurant will not enlarge the space.
findings.verification_note: The cited record references Planning Code § 722, not §780.3(c)(1)(B), and does not contain the specific requirements stated in the sentence.

findings.text: The concept proposes to increase the floor area from 1,486 sq ft to 2,820 sq ft, which is an enlargement, so the condition that the new restaurant will not enlarge the space is not met.
findings.verification_note: The record contains no rule text, floor area numbers, or conditions about enlargement; it only states the controls are in rule lines not shown.

findings.text: Three prior Conditional Use Authorizations are on file at this address: the original 1,000 sq ft restaurant approved in August 1995, expansion to over 2,000 sq ft approved in February 2010, and addition of a full bar approved in December 2003.
The 2010 Conditional Use Authorization (case 2009.0798C) approved expansion of the full-service restaurant for use size over 2,000 sq ft.
findings.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

findings.text: No conditions text is available for the 2009 or 2003 CUAs, and no record in the candidate set since 2010 shows a restaurant square-footage expansion approved in the North Beach Special Use District, so whether current Planning practice permits enlargement despite §780.3(c)(1)(B) is not established.

comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral (not a use decision) shows Planning approved expansion of restaurant service scope on the same block in 2021, though under special legislation. It demonstrates that restaurant use changes in the North Beach SUD have continued to be approved, but through legislation rather than standard CUA process.

conditions: Validity: The authorization and right vested by virtue of this action is valid for three (3) years from the effective date of the Motion. The Department of Building Inspection shall have issued a Building Permit or Site Permit to construct the project and/or commence the approved use within this three-year period. For information about comp liance, contact Code Enforcement, Planning Department at 415 -575-6863, (standard)

Expiration and Renewal: Should a Building or Site Permit be sought after the three (3) year period has lapsed, the project sponsor must seek a renewal of this Authorization by filing an application for an amendment to the original Authorization or a new application for Authorization. Should the project sponsor decline to so file, and decline to withdraw the permit appl ication, the Commission shall conduct a public hearing in order to consider the revocation of the Authorization. (standard)

Diligent Pursuit: Once a site or Buildin g Permit has been issued, construction must commence within the timeframe required by the Department of Building Inspection and be continued diligently to completion. Failure to do so shall be grounds for the Commission to consider revoking the approval if more than three (3) years have passed since this Authorization was approved. (standard)

Extension: All time limits in the preceding three paragraphs may be extended at the discretion of the Zoning Administrator where implementation of the project is delayed by a public agency, an appeal or a legal challenge and only by the length of time for which such public agency, appeal or challenge has caused delay. (standard)

Conformity with Current Law: No application for Building Permit, Site Permit, or other entitlement shall be approved unless it complies with all applicable provisions of City Codes in effect at the time of such approval. DESIGN – COMPLIANCE AT PLAN STAGE (standard)

Garbage, Composting and R ecycling Storage: Space for the collection and storage of garbage, composting, and recycling shall be provided within enclosed areas on the property and clearly labeled and illustrated on the building permit plans. Space for the collection and storage of recyclable and compostable materials that meets the size, location, accessibility and other standards specified by the San Francisco Recycling Program shall be provided at the ground level of the buildings. (standard)

Rooftop Mechanical Equipment: Pursuant to Planning Code 141, the Project Sponsor shall submit a roof plan to the Planning Department prior to Planning approval of the building permit application. Rooftop mechanical equipment, if any is proposed as part of the Project, is required to be screened so as not to be visible from any point at or below the roof level of the subject building. For information about com pliance, contact the Case Planner, Planning Department at 415 -558-6378, (standard)

Odor Control Unit: In order to ensure any significant noxious or offensive odors are prevented from escaping the premi ses once the project is operational, the building permit application to implement the project shall include air cleaning or odor control equipment details and manufacturer specifications on the plans. Odor control ducting shall not be applied to the primary façade of the building. (standard)

Enforcement: Violation of any of the Planning Department conditions of approval contained in this Motion or of any other provisions of Planning Code applicable to this Project shall be subject to the enforcement procedures and administrative penalties set forth under Planning Code Section 176 or Section 176.1. The Planning Department may also refer the violation complaints to other city departments and agencies for appropriate enforcement action under their jurisdiction. (standard)

Revocation due to Violation of Conditions: Should implementation of this Project result in complaints from interested property owners, residents, or commercia l lessees which are not resolved by the Project Sponsor and found to be in violation of the Planning Code and/or the specific conditions of approval for the Project as set forth in Exhibit A of this Motion, the Zoning Administrator shall refer such complaints to the Commission, after which it may hold a public hearing on the matter to consider revocation of this authorization. OPERATION (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (A): The business operator shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Street and Sidewalk Mainte nance Standards. In addition, the operator shall be responsible for daily monitoring of the sidewalk within a one-block radius of the subject business to maintain the sidewalk free of paper or other litter associated with the business during business hours, in accordance with Article 1, Section 34 of the San Francisco Police Code. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (B): When located within an enclosed space, the premises shall be adequately soundproofed or insulated for noise and operated so that incidental noise shall not be audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building, and fixed-source equipment noise shall not exceed the decibel levels specified in the San Francisco Noise Control Ordinance. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (C): While it is inevitable that some low level of odor may be detectable to nearby residents and passersby, appropriate odor control equipment shall be installed in conformance with the approved plans and maintained to prevent any significant noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (D): Garbage, recycling, and compost containers shall be kept within the premises and hidden from public view and placed outside only when being serviced by the disposal company. Trash shall be contained and disposed of pursuant to garbage and recycling receptacles guidelines set forth by the Department of Public Works. Works at 415-554-.5810, http://sfdpw.org. (standard)

Sidewalk Maintenance: The Project Sponsor shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Streets and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. (standard)

Community Liaison: Prior to issuance of a building permit to construct the project and implement the approved use, the Project Sponsor shall appoint a commun ity liaison officer to deal with the issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties. The Project Sponsor shall provide the Zoning Administrator and all registered neighborhood groups for the area with written notice of the name, business address, and telephone number of the community liaison. (standard)
comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant at 526 Columbus (220 meters), same North Beach NCD and SUD. CUA approved adding a full kitchen to an established restaurant in basement and ground floor.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This use decision approved intensification of an existing restaurant (adding full kitchen) in 2020 within the North Beach SUD. Filed July 2019, approved June 2020 (11 months). Standard operational conditions included odor control, noise limits, sidewalk maintenance and community liaison requirements.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant at 653 Union St (145 meters), same North Beach NCD. CUA approved upgrading liquor license from Type 41 to Type 47 in an existing restaurant.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This use decision shows that intensifying an existing restaurant's alcohol service required CUA approval but was granted. Filed October 2015, approved March 2016 (about 4.5 months). Since the current concept serves no alcohol, it avoids this layer of review.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant at 1609 Powell St (174 meters), same North Beach NCD and SUD. Agency referral approving person-to-person transfer of Type 41 ABC license with continuation of existing restaurant use.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral approved in March 2023 shows that ABC license transfers for existing restaurants are routinely approved as continuation of use. However, this is a referral response, not a use decision requiring Commission hearing.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant at 725 Columbus (63 meters, closest candidate), same North Beach NCD and SUD. Agency referral approving ABC License 41 for existing restaurant use (Piccolo Forno).
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral approved in March 2021 shows Planning routinely recommends approval for ABC licenses at established restaurants in the immediate vicinity. However, it is an agency referral for continuation of existing use, not a CUA for physical expansion.

filing_playbook.action: Request a pre-application meeting and a written Letter of Determination from San Francisco Planning Department.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that you propose to expand an existing restaurant at 659 Columbus Ave from 1,486 sq ft to 2,820 sq ft, that the space has been continuously operated as a restaurant since 1995 and was last expanded in 2010 under CUA case 2009.0798C, and ask whether Planning Code §780.3(c)(1)(B) prohibits this expansion and whether any discretionary pathway exists. Request that the planner review the 2010 CUA file and the history of this rule in the North Beach Special Use District. Ask whether the 2010 approval exhausted the right to expand, or whether the rule has been interpreted to allow further enlargement under certain findings.

timeline_cost.notes: No timeline or cost is given because Planning Code §780.3(c)(1)(B) prohibits enlarging an existing restaurant space in the North Beach Special Use District, and the pathway analysis confirms the concept as described is not permitted at this address. The rule lines state that a new restaurant may be approved by Conditional Use only if the Zoning Administrator first finds the new restaurant will not enlarge the space, and the space is to be enlarged from 1,486 sq ft to 2,820 sq ft. The 2010 CUA (case 2009.0798C) approved expansion to over 2,000 sq ft, but no record in the candidate set since 2010 shows a restaurant square-footage expansion approved under this rule, and the current rule text does not provide an exception for existing restaurants. Until Planning confirms in writing whether any discretionary pathway exists, no application should be filed and no cost or timeline for approval can be estimated. If Planning confirms there is no approval path, the only options are to operate within the existing 1,486 sq ft footprint, seek a legislative amendment to the North Beach SUD, or choose a different location.

records_summary: 659 Columbus Ave operates as Piazza Pellegrini, a full-service restaurant with an active Type 47 liquor license that has been continuously permitted since 1995. The site history shows three prior Conditional Use Authorizations: the original 1,000 sq ft restaurant in 1995, expansion to over 2,000 sq ft in 2009, and addition of a full bar in 2003. The North Beach Special Use District rule at Planning Code §780.3(c)(1)(B) explicitly prohibits a restaurant from enlarging its existing space, which the pathway analysis confirms makes this proposed 1,486 sq ft to 2,820 sq ft expansion "not permitted" even though the restaurant use itself continues. The immediate area is densely packed with 20 food/drink businesses and 11 on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, with 42 licenses within 1,000 ft.
